subject: Data Analysis Menu using Shiny - Version 0.01

messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: Data Analysis Menu using Shiny - Version 0.01
parts:
I put a pre-alpha data-analysis menu on github (https://github.com/mostly-harmless/damshiny.git). I also posted it as a Gist. The following should work, if not please let me know.

library(shiny)
shiny::runGist('4385800')

I have a number of questions and would love to hear suggestions for improvement. If you would like to contribute directly, even better.

1. Main question: Does the structure I used in server.R make sense? Is it (reasonably) efficients? If not how could efficiency be enhanced? Note that I plan to add 10-15 more 'tools' to the menu once the basic code-structure is a bit more solid.
2. Errors are printed when data or variables have not yet been selected. Is there a clean way to avoid this across various functions?
2. I saw some discussion about conditional tabs but it wasn't clear to me how to implement this. Suggestions?
3. How to provide a list of data.frames in memory available for analysis? I tried sapply(mget(ls(),.GlobalEnv),is.data.frame) but couldn't get it to work inside the shiny app.
4. Plots don't show completely (have to scroll). Is there a way to make the output window longer?
5. Is it possible to make the window for a selectInput with multiple=TRUE longer (e.g., height based on the number of variables in a data.frame)?
6. If a variable has been selected as a dependent variable could that easily be removed from the list of independent variables?
7. Can dropdowns in shiny have sub-menu's (e.g. regression could have, say, two sub-options: linear and logistic). I could put-in a conditional selectInput I guess.
8. For larger datasets I might want to turn-off reactive features. Is that possible and if so how?

messages.subject: Re: Data Analysis Menu using Shiny - Version 0.01
parts:
The Data Analysis Menu using Shiny (version 0.03) is now on Glimmer (http://glimmer.rstudio.com/mostlyhrmls/damshiny/). Since loading user data is experimental on Shiny Server I disabled it on Glimmer. If you want to try it out with your own data you will need to run the app locally. The source code for the app is at https://github.com/mostly-harmless/damshiny with some basic install instructions. Shiny does not run in IE so neither will damshiny. Try Chrome or Firefox.

Comments & suggestions are welcome.
